UnitStatement: TYPES.md is the authoritative vocabulary reference for the Chirality project execution system.
TYPES.md defines canonical entities, stable identifier formats, enumerated types, agent roles, and lifecycle states.
All agents and governance documents use the terms defined in TYPES.md.
When a term is used differently elsewhere, TYPES.md governs.
The project hierarchy is flat: packages contain deliverables.
The project hierarchy has no phases, sub-packages, or task sub-levels within deliverables.
Package folders live directly under EXECUTION_ROOT using `PKG-XX_{PkgLabel}`.
Deliverable folders live under `{PKG}/1_Working/` using `DEL-XX-YY_{DelLabel}`.
A package is a flat partition of project scope.
Packages do not nest.
Every scope item belongs to exactly one package.
Package coverage has no overlaps or gaps.
Packages are defined by PROJECT_DECOMP.
Packages are confirmed by the human.
A deliverable is a unit of production within a package.
Each deliverable belongs to exactly one package.
Each deliverable has a responsible party.
Each deliverable has a type.
Each deliverable produces one or more anticipated artifacts.
Each deliverable occupies one folder under `{PKG}/1_Working/`.
An artifact is a tangible output produced within a deliverable folder.
Artifacts include the document kit: Datasheet, Specification, Guidance, and Procedure.
Artifacts may include additional outputs appropriate to the deliverable type.
Identifiers are assigned once.
Identifiers persist across renames, path changes, and restructuring.
Path is a physical projection of the decomposition, not identity itself.
Package IDs use format `PKG-XX`.
Package IDs are assigned by PROJECT_DECOMP.
Deliverable IDs use format `DEL-XX-YY`.
Deliverable IDs are assigned by PROJECT_DECOMP.
Dependency IDs use format `DEP-XX-YY-NNN`.
Dependency IDs are assigned by TASK+dependency-extract.
Scope Item IDs use format `SOW-NNN`.
Scope Item IDs are assigned by PROJECT_DECOMP.
Objective IDs use format `OBJ-NNN`.
Objective IDs are assigned by PROJECT_DECOMP.
`XX` in package IDs is a zero-padded numeric sequence.
`YY` in deliverable IDs is a zero-padded numeric sequence scoped to the package.
`NNN` in dependency IDs is a zero-padded numeric sequence scoped to the deliverable.
IDs MUST NOT change across revisions unless the human explicitly requests renumbering.
Deliverable IDs use hyphen separators.
Deliverable IDs do not use dot separators.
Folder names combine the stable ID with a human-readable label.
Package folder label format is `{PKG-ID}_{Sanitize(PackageName)}`.
Deliverable folder label format is `{DEL-ID}_{Sanitize(DeliverableName)}`.
The canonical unsanitized name is recorded in `_CONTEXT.md`.
Sanitization rules are defined in `SPEC.md` Section 10.
Dependencies capture relationships between deliverables, definition nodes, and external entities.
The dependency model distinguishes two fundamental edge classes.
ANCHOR connects a deliverable to a definition or traceability node.
ANCHOR is a vertical tree edge.
EXECUTION captures information flow, prerequisites, handoffs, and constraints between work items.
EXECUTION is a horizontal DAG edge.
ANCHOR and EXECUTION together form a knowledge graph.
In the knowledge graph, the tree preserves stable intent.
In the knowledge graph, the DAG captures execution couplings.
IMPLEMENTS_NODE is the parent definition node anchor type.
Each deliverable has exactly one IMPLEMENTS_NODE anchor.
TRACES_TO_REQUIREMENT is a requirement trace link anchor type.
Each deliverable may have zero or more TRACES_TO_REQUIREMENT anchors.
NOT_APPLICABLE is used only for EXECUTION rows.
Dependency direction is always relative to the host deliverable.
UPSTREAM means the host deliverable requires information from the target.
DOWNSTREAM means the host deliverable produces information for the target.
Legacy value INBOUND normalizes to UPSTREAM.
Legacy value OUTBOUND normalizes to DOWNSTREAM.
PREREQUISITE is an Execution dependency representing required input or approval before work can proceed.
INTERFACE is an Execution dependency for explicit data or artifact exchange between deliverables.
HANDOVER is an Execution dependency where one deliverable's output is consumed as input to another.
CONSTRAINT is an Execution dependency for an explicit constraint or condition.
ENABLES is an Execution dependency where a deliverable enables downstream work.
OTHER is the default for ANCHOR rows.
OTHER is a catch-all for EXECUTION rows.
Legacy type COORDINATION MUST NOT be emitted in new extractions.
Legacy type INFORMATION MUST NOT be emitted in new extractions.
DELIVERABLE target type means another deliverable in the project.
PACKAGE target type means a package.
WBS_NODE target type means a work breakdown structure or scope node.
REQUIREMENT target type means a specific requirement such as a SOW item or objective.
DOCUMENT target type means an external or reference document.
EQUIPMENT target type means physical equipment or asset.
EXTERNAL target type means an external entity such as an organization or standard.
UNKNOWN target type means the target cannot be confidently resolved.
Explicitness records whether a dependency is directly stated in source text.
Explicitness values are EXPLICIT and IMPLICIT.
Confidence records the strength of evidence supporting a dependency.
Confidence values are HIGH, MEDIUM, and LOW.
Origin records human-declared versus agent-extracted provenance.
Origin values are DECLARED and EXTRACTED.
SatisfactionStatus tracks whether a dependency has been fulfilled.
SatisfactionStatus values are TBD, PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, SATISFIED, WAIVED, and NOT_APPLICABLE.
Status tracks whether a dependency is currently observed in sources.
Status values are ACTIVE and RETIRED.
Agents are classified into three types following the 0-1-2 model.
Type 0 agents are named Architect.
Type 0 agents define and maintain standards, contracts, and role boundaries.
Type 0 agents have project-wide scope.
Type 1 agents are named Manager.
Type 1 agents interpret intent, decompose work, route to specialists, and merge results.
Type 1 agents operate at package or project scope.
Type 2 agents are named Specialist.
Type 2 agents execute bounded briefs with minimal context.
Type 2 agents return outputs and evidence.
Type 2 agents operate at a single deliverable or narrow task scope.
AGENT_CLASS values are PERSONA and TASK.
PERSONA agents run interactive sessions.
TASK agents run straight-through pipelines.
INTERACTION_SURFACE records how an agent is invoked.
INTERACTION_SURFACE values are chat, INIT-TASK, spawned, and both.
WRITE_SCOPE records what an agent is allowed to write.
WRITE_SCOPE values are repo-wide, deliverable-local, tool-root-only, workspace-scaffold-only, repo-metadata-only, and none.
BLOCKING records whether an agent may pause for human input.
BLOCKING values are never and allowed.
Type 0 proposes rules defining what correct means.
Type 1 prepares workspaces and orchestrates what the specialist can see.
Type 2 does the work within bounded scope.
Humans approve at gates.
Authority flows downward.
Escalation flows upward.
A Type 2 agent cannot modify rules set by Type 0.
A Type 1 agent cannot approve deliverables for external reliance.
The deliverable lifecycle sequence is OPEN -> INITIALIZED -> SEMANTIC_READY -> IN_PROGRESS -> CHECKING -> ISSUED.
OPEN means a folder exists with the minimum viable fileset and no content yet.
INITIALIZED means the document kit has been drafted.
SEMANTIC_READY means semantic lens `_SEMANTIC.md` has been generated.
IN_PROGRESS means active human and agent work is underway.
CHECKING means the deliverable is under review.
ISSUED means the deliverable has been released for use.
Lifecycle states are tracked in `_STATUS.md`.
Lifecycle states represent the deliverable's production status.
Stage gates are human-managed milestones representing project-level progress checkpoints.
Stage gates are not lifecycle states.
Stage gates are tracked separately in coordination records.
The INITIALIZED to SEMANTIC_READY transition is optional.
If semantic lensing is skipped, deliverables may transition directly from INITIALIZED to IN_PROGRESS.
The framework separates how teams coordinate from how the system tracks dependencies.
The system always maintains deliverable-local dependency registers.
SCHEDULE_FIRST means Gantt drives sequencing.
In SCHEDULE_FIRST mode, dependency tracking remains active for blocker detection and audit.
DEPENDENCY_TRACKED means the dependency graph drives sequencing.
HYBRID combines schedule-first and dependency-tracked coordination.
Coordination representation is recorded in `_COORDINATION.md`.
Coordination representation is chosen per project instance.
Each deliverable contains a standard four-document kit.
Datasheet.md records key parameters, identification, and structured metadata.
Specification.md records technical requirements, scope definition, and acceptance criteria.
Guidance.md records design guidance, rationale, best practices, and contextual direction.
Procedure.md records step-by-step execution workflow, sequencing, and checklists.
The project decomposition document is produced by PROJECT_DECOMP.
The project decomposition document defines additional decomposition entities.
Scope Item uses ID format `SOW-NNN`.
Scope Item is an atomic, testable scope statement from the Structured Scope of Work.
Objective uses ID format `OBJ-NNN`.
Objective is a success criterion derived from scope and mapped to supporting deliverables.
Vocabulary Map is a table of canonical terms and synonyms to prevent semantic drift.
Scope Ledger is a machine-checkable mapping of every scope item to packages and deliverables.
Coverage & Telemetry summarize metrics, gaps, and open issues that make decomposition quality measurable.
The desktop frontend uses canonical UI terms for matrix routing and pipeline selection state.
MatrixRow values are NORMATIVE, OPERATIVE, and EVALUATIVE.
MatrixRow is the major intent lane used for routing to WORKBENCH or PIPELINE.
MatrixColumn values are GUIDING, APPLYING, JUDGING, and REVIEWING.
MatrixColumn is the role-oriented matrix column shared across all rows.
PipelineCategory values are DECOMP*, PREP*, TASK*, and AUDIT*.
PipelineCategory is the top-level pipeline mode selected in the header.
TaskScopeMode values are DELIVERABLES and KNOWLEDGE_TYPES.
TaskScopeMode is a dynamic scope mode used only when PipelineCategory=TASK*.
Knowledge decomposition marker is a decomposition-document signal enabling knowledge-type scope in TASK selectors.
Knowledge decomposition marker examples include headings or phrases containing Knowledge Categories, Knowledge Types, or equivalent marker text.
Knowledge type option is a canonical file-type bucket returned by API scanning and selectable in TASK scope mode.
Knowledge type option examples include Datasheet, Specification, Guidance, Procedure, Dependencies, References, Context, Status, Semantic, and Memory.
The epistemology pillar operates on formally defined entities.
The epistemic ontology contains entities acted on by provenance, no-invention, conflict-surfacing, and epistemic-labeling mechanisms.
Claim is an assertion that something is the case.
Claim is the atomic unit of epistemology.
Every non-trivial assertion produced by an agent in a governed workflow is a claim.
Claim canonical locations include dependency rows, document content, and agent outputs.
Warrant is the justification for believing a claim.
Warrant is always extrinsic.
Warrant may be a source citation containing file, section, and quote.
Warrant is never intrinsic model confidence or plausibility.
Warrant canonical locations include EvidenceFile, SourceRef, and EvidenceQuote columns in Dependencies.csv.
Status is the epistemic classification of claim certainty.
Status is expressed as one of four labels.
Status canonical locations include Notes fields, dependency records, and agent output prose.
Gap is the explicit positive assertion that a warrant has not been found.
Gap is not the absence of information.
Gap represents absence and makes it visible and actionable.
Gap canonical locations include TBD markers, location TBD in provenance fields, and open issues.
Conflict is two or more claims with incompatible warrants about the same key.
Conflict itself is an epistemic entity.
Conflict must be resolved before the deliverable can advance.
Conflict canonical locations include Conflict Tables with ConflictID, Key, Contenders, ProposedAuthority, and HumanRuling.
Ruling is a human decision that resolves a gap or conflict.
Ruling transforms epistemic status.
Rulings are binding and recorded in versioned files.
Ruling canonical locations include HumanRuling column in Conflict Tables, finding dispositions in REVIEW, and gate decisions.
A claim has exactly one status: FACT, ASSUMPTION, PROPOSAL, or TBD.
A claim may have a warrant with source file, section reference, and optional quote.
Absence of warrant is structurally visible for claims.
A claim without warrant is a gap.
A claim without warrant has status TBD or uncited PROPOSAL.
Absence of warrant is itself a finding.
Two claims may be in conflict when they share the same key, have incompatible values, and come from different sources.
A conflict requires a ruling.
HumanRuling remains TBD until the licensed professional adjudicates a conflict.
A ruling transforms status by resolving gaps, accepting or rejecting proposals, and resolving conflicts.
Resolving a gap changes status from TBD to FACT or ASSUMPTION.
Resolving a conflict changes competing claims into one accepted claim.
Four epistemic labels classify claim certainty status.
FACT means directly observed in source text with citation.
FACT reviewer action is to verify the citation and accept if the source is authoritative.
ASSUMPTION means reasonable inference grounded in cited material but not directly stated.
ASSUMPTION requires validation or rejection and a documented decision.
PROPOSAL means suggested interpretation, action, or design move.
PROPOSAL may cite supporting context.
PROPOSAL requires a human decision to become binding.
TBD means an unknown placeholder requiring resolution.
TBD must be resolved before reliance.
Claims within a deliverable progress through a warrant lifecycle.
The warrant lifecycle tracks epistemic state.
The warrant lifecycle is interleaved with the deliverable lifecycle.
The warrant lifecycle sequence is UNWARRANTED -> CITED -> REVIEWED -> AUTHENTICATED.
UNWARRANTED means a claim exists but has no source citation.
UNWARRANTED status is TBD or uncited PROPOSAL.
UNWARRANTED transition mechanism is agent claim production with K-INVENT-1 requiring TBD marking for gaps.
CITED means a claim has a source citation.
CITED status is FACT, ASSUMPTION, or cited PROPOSAL.
CITED transition mechanism is agent-attached provenance enforced by K-PROV-1.
REVIEWED means a claim has been examined by a licensed professional.
REVIEWED findings have been dispositioned.
REVIEWED transition mechanism is REVIEW gates and human rulings on findings.
AUTHENTICATED means a claim is part of an authenticated PWP.
In AUTHENTICATED state, the professional warrants the claim under duty of care.
AUTHENTICATED transition mechanism is authentication binding to git SHA enforced by K-AUTH-2.
The deliverable lifecycle asks what state the work product is in.
The warrant lifecycle asks what state the knowledge about the work product is in.
A deliverable is ready for issuance when its warrants are sufficient.
Warrants are sufficient when the licensed professional determines that claim epistemic state supports authentication under professional responsibility.
The deliverable lifecycle and warrant lifecycle are correlated but not identical.
A deliverable in IN_PROGRESS contains a mixture of warranted and unwarranted claims.
Transition to CHECKING requires critical claims to have been warranted.
Critical claims are warranted when all CRITICAL findings have non-TBD human disposition.
Transition to ISSUED requires professional authentication of the work.
Professional authentication warrants deliverable claims under professional responsibility.
K-PROV-1 mandatory provenance governs Warrant.
K-PROV-1 requires every claim to have an extrinsic warrant or explicit location TBD.
K-INVENT-1 no invention governs Gap.
K-INVENT-1 requires missing data to be represented as a gap, not fabricated.
K-CONFLICT-1 conflict surfacing governs Conflict.
K-CONFLICT-1 requires disagreements to be exposed as conflicts, not silently resolved.
K-AUTH-1 human authority governs Ruling.
K-AUTH-1 means only humans may author binding rulings and approval records.
K-AUTH-2 SHA-bound approval governs Authentication.
K-AUTH-2 means warrant-to-content binding is mechanically verifiable.
